# GitKraken Reviews

### The community submitted 13 reviews to tell us what they like about GitKraken, what GitKraken can do better, and more.

Based on 13 reviews

Review GitKraken?

Reviewers largely praise GitKraken for making Git easier to understand and use, especially through its clear visual commit graph, visual conflict resolution, drag-and-drop history editing, line-by-line staging, and GitHub pull request integration. Several say it lowers stress on complex tasks and even helps beginners get started quickly. But the praise is tempered by sharp complaints about reliability, support, and product direction: a few users report serious bugs, hidden file changes, inconsistent behavior, frustration with added AI features, and pricing that feels hard to justify for light use.

results.title: git-lrc: Free, unlimited AI code reviews that run on commit | Product Hunt
results.content:
I prototyped git-lrc such that AI helps the developer work through diffs faster, acquire an understanding of what's going on, and fix issues on a commit-by-commit basis.  
  
git-lrc was built with the idea that review shouldn’t be an afterthought. It should be structurally encouraged while putting the developer in control.

So in git-lrc, while a review is triggered automatically, the dev can still consciously skip the review. [...] Or they can manually review and "vouch" for the change they are making.  
  
All these micro review decisions get recorded in git log—for future analysis so that the team could operate at higher engineering standards.  
  
As to git-lrc, it takes 60 seconds to set up and is completely free for any number of reviews—thanks to Google Gemini's Free tier.  
  
I encourage you to give git-lrc a try and see the difference in the quality of your code as well as concrete outcomes such as reduced production bugs.

git-lrc

git-lrc

git-lrc started from a practical observation within my own team.

As our usage of AI coding tools like Copilot, Cursor, etc., increased, our velocity seemingly went up—but careful checking of the AI-generated code went down.

Engineers were committing code they hadn’t truly examined.

Reviews were happening later, sometimes too late, and often superficially (because AI generates tons of code)

This led to abstruse bugs and long debugging at prod.

Clearly, we needed a solution.  
  
I didn’t want another dashboard. I wanted a strong nudge to review code at the right place—exactly where responsibility is bound to exist: git commit.

Review Fork?

Reviewers largely praise Fork for a native-feeling, well-designed Git workflow that is fast, intuitive, and easy to fold into daily work. Several call out its smooth handling of complex Git tasks, with one user saying it is especially useful for large PR diffs. A maker of Lista echoes that, describing it as clean, fast, reliable, and open every day beside Xcode. The main tension is not the app itself but one user’s sharply negative experience with the lead developer’s combative issue-tracker responses.
